messages.subject: Batch timeout based upon batch size?
messages.subject_clean: Batch timeout based upon batch size?
messages.body_plain:
I'm using simmer 4.4.3 and have been able to define a batch size based upon an attribute in the arrivals dataframe. It is a simulation of a warehouse unloading dock.  A group of pallets (quantity varies) batch together, "seize" a truck and a unloading dock, then use them for a time that is roughly proportional to the batch size, with some variability.  Here is the code so far:

pallets_trajectory <- trajectory("pallets_movement") %>%
batch(n= function() {get_attribute(warehouse_env, "Inbound_Batch_Size")}, permanent=FALSE) %>%
#the batch of pallets "seizes" a truck and a dock simultneously
seize("truck",1) %>%
seize("dock",1) %>%
#need to replace this timeout
timeout(10)

Is there some way to just retrieve the batch size as an attribute, so I can make that part of a function inside timeout()?

messages.body_plain:
On Tue, 14 Sept 2021 at 04:13, Ralph Asher <ralph....@gmail.com> wrote:
> I'm using simmer 4.4.3 and have been able to define a batch size based upon an attribute in the arrivals dataframe. It is a simulation of a warehouse unloading dock.  A group of pallets (quantity varies) batch together, "seize" a truck and a unloading dock, then use them for a time that is roughly proportional to the batch size, with some variability.  Here is the code so far:
>
> pallets_trajectory <- trajectory("pallets_movement") %>%
> batch(n= function() {get_attribute(warehouse_env, "Inbound_Batch_Size")}, permanent=FALSE) %>%
> #the batch of pallets "seizes" a truck and a dock simultneously
> seize("truck",1) %>%
> seize("dock",1) %>%
> #need to replace this timeout
> timeout(10)
>
> Is there some way to just retrieve the batch size as an attribute, so I can make that part of a function inside timeout()?

Unfortunately, no, there's no way. We would need to implement a new getter for this parameter. I'll add this as a feature request to the repo.

Currently, you could use a global, e.g.

t <- trajectory() %>%
  set_global("attr", 1) %>%
  batch(function() get_global(env, "attr")) %>%
  log_(function() paste0(get_global(env, "attr")))

But you need to be careful to avoid overwriting it

--
Iñaki Úcar

messages.body_plain:
Not sure I understand the use of a global here.  I am already successfully defining different batch sizes using the pallet arrivals data frame as part of the pallets trajectory.

 For example, the first 20 pallets all have the same arrival time t=0 because they arrive on the same truck at t=0, and seize a truck and loading dock as a batch.  After the unload activity timeout, they separate.  The next 15 pallets have an arrival time of t=60, representing the arrival time of the second truck.

Could I overwrite a global attribute with each batch that holds the batch size, then retrieve that global in a function within timeout?

messages.body_plain:
On Tue, 14 Sept 2021 at 14:17, Ralph Asher <ralph....@gmail.com> wrote:
> Not sure I understand the use of a global here.  I am already successfully defining different batch sizes using the pallet arrivals data frame as part of the pallets trajectory.

The thing is, if you set an attribute before entering the batch, the batch cannot access that attribute in the timeout, because it belongs to an individual arrival that is inside the batch. E.g.:

> t <- trajectory() %>%

+   set_attribute("attr", 1) %>%
+   batch(function() get_attribute(env, "attr")) %>%
+   log_(function() paste0(get_attribute(env, "attr")))
>
> env <- simmer() %>%
+   add_generator("dummy", t, at(0))
>
> env %>%
+   run() %>%
+   invisible()
0: batch0: NA

prints NA, because "attr" is not defined for the batch. On the other hand, globals can be accessed from anywhere:

> t <- trajectory() %>%

+   set_global("attr", 1) %>%
+   batch(function() get_global(env, "attr")) %>%
+   log_(function() paste0(get_global(env, "attr")))
>
> env <- simmer() %>%
+   add_generator("dummy", t, at(0))
>
> env %>%
+   run() %>%
+   invisible
0: batch0: 1

Iñaki
